title: Synthesis of Resource-Efficient Superconducting Circuits with Clock-Free Alternating Logic
problem: Gate-level clocking in traditional Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) technology requires ad hoc modifications to synthesis tools and creates significant engineering barriers to automation. The clock dependency embedded in gate semantics prevents straightforward application of standard logic synthesis approaches to superconducting circuits.
motivation: Superconducting circuits offer ultra-low-power computing potential, and removing synthesis automation barriers is critical for practical development and scaling of SFQ-based systems.
method: The paper introduces xSFQ (alternating SFQ), a logic family using dual-rail alternating encoding to eliminate clock dependency from gate operations. This encoding scheme enables clock-free gate semantics without ad hoc modifications to existing synthesis tools. The approach is integrated into automated synthesis workflows to optimize circuit resource usage and reduce overhead.
key_novelty: Dual-rail alternating encoding (xSFQ) for eliminating clock dependency in superconducting gates, enabling fully automated clock-free synthesis of SFQ circuits.
contributions: Introduction of xSFQ logic family for clock-free superconducting circuit synthesis
Removal of clock dependency from gate semantics, eliminating ad hoc synthesis tool modifications
80% average reduction in Josephson junction count on ISCAS85, EPFL, and ISCAS89 benchmarks
Simplified automated design flow for resource-efficient superconducting circuits
